Let the odd-indexed terms be \(a_1,a_3,\dots,a_{2n+1}\), giving \(n+1\) terms, and the even-indexed terms be \(a_2,a_4,\dots,a_{2n}\), giving \(n\) terms.

Both sets are arithmetic sequences with common difference \(2d\). Their sums are:

\[
S_{\text{odd}}=(n+1)(a_1+nd)=132
\]
\[
S_{\text{even}}=n(a_1+nd)=120
\]

Subtracting:

\[
(a_1+nd)=132-120=12
\]

Then:

\[
12n=120 \implies n=10
\]

\[
\boxed{10}
\]
